_doc: World art (pixel art, the custom-mode design studio's look). gen.ps1 draws each sheet with the image model into sheets/ (style = DesignAi.Style / TileStyle); the Unity menu Diverse/Art/Import Painted Art pixelizes them into Assets/_Project/Resources/Sprites/<key>.png (16 px per tile, every dot dotScale px wide). fit: w = width in tiles, h = height in tiles. pivotY: where the object's base sits, as a fraction of its height from the bottom.
style: Cute pixel art video game sprite, 16-bit style, chunky readable silhouette, bold dark outline, flat cel shading, limited soft colour palette, simple shapes with little detail, no text, no ground, no cast shadow, isolated on a fully transparent background. Scenery objects for a top-down game world, standing upright, front view.
sheetStyle: A sprite sheet laid out as an even {cols} x {rows} grid, read left to right then top to bottom; exactly one object centered in each cell, all objects at a consistent scale relative to each other, generous empty space between objects, nothing touching another object or the cell edges.
groundStyle: Top-down pixel art video game terrain textures, 16-bit style, flat lighting, no objects, no shadows, no perspective, no text. A 2x2 grid of four square texture swatches filling the whole image edge to edge, no borders or gaps, read left to right then top to bottom. Each swatch is subtle and low contrast: one main colour with fine detail, no big shapes, no grid lines, no checkerboard.
